text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The resumption of parliamentary life with the last session of parliament on Tuesday:King Hussein reviews key achievements and the "characteristics of the coming stage."
- Justice minister says state has released all those implicated in the events of the south (arrested during outbreak of troubles in August on doubling of bread prices).
- The start of the trial of the killer of his two children.
- King Hussein opens the last session of parliament on Tuesday, the throne's speech emphasises "steadfast" Jordanian positions and the elections law.
- King Hussein says "we have succeeded in making bridges with international blocs and our role is prominent in consolidating the basis of comprehensive peace in the region."
- Prime Minister Kabariti inaugurates festivities in Karak on the occassion of the king's birthday, says "the government lives your suffering and aspirations."
- Kabariti says "we have prevented the deterioration of the economic situation..there was a need for a courageous confrontation, curbing spending and corruption."
- Jordan urges Iraq to disclose identity of killers of its embassy driver last week.
- A study on the lgal implications of the ruling by U.S. President Clinton on classifying Jordan as a key ally.
- Emirates employs 300 Jordanians to work there.
- King hails Jordan's status as non-NATO ally of U.S.
- Audit bureau reports civil service embezzelement of 718,920 dinars ($101,542) in 1995.
